subtitle: Ring on the side rail + a C-grip on the angled strut whose closed wall faces the cup · no screw · a full cup pushes the grip on tighter · shown assembled in its real orientation (rail left to right) · millimetres

scale_note: Real size, shown assembled in its real orientation: the rail runs left to right, the cup stands upright and hangs off the outside of it. The rail is your 22.3 mm tube; the angled strut is your 13.5 mm square bar, drawn as a straight line at ~59° from the tape photos (so it is accurate to roughly a few mm). The gap between the rail and the strut is the least certain number (4 to 7 mm, drawn at 5.5). The tumbler is from retailer listings. The wireframe blocks are the red latch zones (approximate).
notes_title: What changed, and what to check
notes: v9: a mirrored clip for the left-hand side, so a cup holder can go on either side of the wagon. The left clip (wagon-cup-clip-left.stl) is the right clip's mirror image: viewed from outside with the cup toward you, the right clip's arm goes to the left and the left clip's arm goes to the right, always toward the strut's pivot end. The cup module is the same part for both sides (it is symmetric). The viewer shows the right clip; turn on 'LEFT-side clip' and 'Angled strut, left frame' to compare (they sit on the same rail, so hide the right clip and strut to see the left one alone). Please check: (1) is the left frame really a mirror of the right (strut from the same end relative to the push handle)? (2) print the left clip with supports and try it on the left frame.
